spots.label: evisceration trough rim (stainless)
spots.vla_note: Zone 1. Swab the flat top of the rim, not the inside wall, so the swab stays on stainless.
spots.justification: evisceration trough rim (stainless) [Zone 1 (food-contact)]. VLM risk prior 0.88 (factors: product contact, water + offal, weld seams). Reachable from base pose x=14.68, y=3.56, yaw=0 deg with manipulability 0.51, 21 cm arm clearance and 4/4 raster corners of the 10x10 cm patch reachable. Utility 0.298 = risk^2 x feasibility x novelty 1.00 x travel(7.2 m); it was #2 of the top 8 in the Zone-1/2/3 pool and was drawn with probability 0.37 (randomised risk-based sampling, seed 7).

decision.justification: Swab the evisceration-trough rim (candidate 113) first. It is a Zone-1 food-contact surface (offal and water run along it, and weld seams along the lip are a known harbourage point), it has the highest utility of all reachable spots (0.397) and its image (node view) confirms the 10x10 cm patch sits on the flat stainless lip, not on the hose beside it. Reachability is good: manipulability 0.51, 21 cm arm clearance, all 4 raster corners reachable. I changed the engine's visiting order from 113-50-407-19-492 to 113-407-492-50-19: sampling must go from clean to dirty (Zone 1, then 2, then 3) so the robot and its tooling do not carry drain contamination onto food-contact or near-product surfaces. The trench drain under the trough (19) has the highest raw risk (0.90) but is last for that reason, and it is the most diagnostic Zone-3 site because it receives the trough discharge. The overhead shackles (risk 0.88-0.92) are the true top-risk Zone-1 sites, but 145 of 146 shackle candidates are 1.4-2.4 m high and outside UR5e reach from any drivable Husky pose, so they must be swabbed manually or by a lift-mounted tool; this is reported, not ignored.
abort_conditions: Contact force exceeds 25 N or no contact within 3 cm past the expected surface (map error).
A person or obstacle is closer than 1 m to the arm workspace (safety-rated scanner zone).
Base localisation covariance exceeds 5 cm before a Zone-1 approach.
Live depth shows the surface more than 4 cm from the map (equipment has moved).
Plan order would visit Zone 1 after Zone 3 with the same tooling.

action_plan.detail: Move UR5e to the stow pose from husky.srdf before driving.
Drive the A* path to the base pose for candidate 113 (pose from data/swab_plan.json).
Place the swab tip 10 cm off the rim along its surface normal.
Move straight in along -normal at 2 cm/s until contact (force threshold ~10 N on the real robot).
Zig-zag 5 passes across the 10x10 cm patch, then rotate the swab and repeat perpendicular.
Bag the swab; record site id, zone, time and pose. Load a fresh swab.
Stow the arm and continue with 407, 492, 50, 19 in that order, repeating steps 2-8.

rejected.reason: Same trough rim 0.4 m from 113; would duplicate coverage (novelty penalty).
Shackle carousel body: high risk but no depth-confirmed image of the patch and complex wire geometry; a flat 10x10 cm swab cannot be guaranteed.
Combo bin side wall duplicates candidate 407 on the same bin.
Trench drain section with no confirming image; 19 covers the same drain where the organic load is highest.
